scope.object: Uncommitted working-tree changes to tools/audit_core_no_vendor_dll.py and validation/test_audit_core_no_vendor_dll.py (the three P1 fixes responding to validation/coordination/codebuddy-core-native-audit-review-20260913-01)
scope.mode: adversarial read-only; pure AST + tempdir fixtures; no native loads, no .so/.dll bytes, no ROS/flight-control/model/UE/MATLAB, no process control

verdict.summary: All three P1 fixes are NOT fail-closed. 15 of 17 repro cases bypass the new checks while the audit reports status=pass with zero violations; both controls (baseline pass, second-CDLL rejection) behave correctly, so the audit is alive but the new exception validation remains presence-based, not semantic.

runs.result: 17 cases: 2 controls correct, 15 bypasses (audit pass where fail expected)
status=pass, violations=[] on the real working tree

findings.title: Gate effectiveness fix is walk-based and reachability-blind: unreachable raise, dead outer condition, dead nested def, and swallowed raise all satisfy the gates
findings.location: tools/audit_core_no_vendor_dll.py: _if_body_raises (324-327), gate scan in _perf_recorder_load_shape_ok (449-498), lexical check at 452
findings.root_cause: ast.walk descends into any nesting depth. _if_body_raises accepts a Raise buried in an inner `if False:` / nested def; the gate scan accepts an If nested under a dead outer `if False:`, inside a never-called nested def, or inside a try whose except swallows the raise; `node.lineno < call.lineno` is lexical order, not dominance. _gate_test_intact only inspects the gate's own test, so neutralization one level up or down is invisible.

repro_cases.A1_digest_gate_unreachable_raise: perf_capture.py:40 -> `            if False: raise PerfCaptureError('Perf library SHA256 mismatch')` (one line, digest gate never fires: any content passes)
repro_cases.A2_path_gate_unreachable_raise: perf_capture.py:31 -> `            if False: raise ...` (one line, path gate never fires: relative/non-.so/nonexistent paths pass)
repro_cases.A3_sha_gate_unreachable_raise: perf_capture.py:34 -> `            if False: raise ...` (one line, SHA shape gate never fires)
repro_cases.B_digest_gate_under_dead_outer_if: lines 39-40 -> outer `if False:` wrapping the intact digest gate (2 lines for 2, pinned line 51 holds)
repro_cases.F_gates_inside_dead_nested_def: lines 30-40 -> never-called nested `def _verify(...)` holding all gates + digest feed; top level keeps only `library = Path(library_path)` and the pinned load: fully unverified dlopen with audit green
repro_cases.G_digest_gate_raise_swallowed: lines 39-40 -> `try: <intact gate> / except PerfCaptureError: pass` (line-neutral via merging lines 47-50)

findings.observed: all six cases report status=pass, violations=[]; semantically each disables at least one gate while loading anyway
findings.impact: The three new tests (and-False, raise->pass, reorder) only cover exact-token deletion and whole-block reorder. Token-preserving reachability attacks defeat every gate; F defeats all gates and the digest binding at once. The docstring claim 'every gate dominates the load' is false.
minimal_fix: Require each gate If to be a DIRECT element of the host function's body sequence (iterate function.body in order; do not ast.walk for gate discovery), and require the pinned CDLL statement to appear later in that same sequence. Gates nested in If/Try/While/For/FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef/ClassDef fail closed.

Replace _if_body_raises with an exact-shape check: the gate body must be exactly one unconditional ast.Raise (optionally preceded by a constant-docstring Expr). Any nested compound statement in the body fails closed.
Optionally also reject a gate whose Raise type is caught by an enclosing try in the same function (or simpler: reject gates not at top level, which already covers the try case).

findings.title: Digest/path dataflow fix lacks binding-count and read-size constraints: vacuous read(0), path rebinding after verification, digest rebinding all pass
findings.location: tools/audit_core_no_vendor_dll.py: token scan 381-413, feed check 416-444 (read size never inspected at 425-430; no uniqueness/no-rebind check for path_name/digest_name/stream_name)
findings.root_cause: The feed loop is matched structurally (lambda calls <stream>.read, sentinel b'', update(chunk)) but the read size argument is never validated, and no check requires the verified names to be bound exactly once or forbids rebinding between verification and load.

repro_cases.C_vacuous_read_zero: perf_capture.py:37 read(1024 * 1024) -> read(0): the iter() sentinel fires immediately, zero file bytes are hashed, digest is the empty-input hash (one-line edit; same class as the fixed digest.update(b''))
repro_cases.D_path_rebound_after_verify: perf_capture.py:47 -> `        self.library_path = str(library); library = Path('/tmp/evil.so')` (one-line edit): all gates and the digest run on the caller's genuine file, then line 51 dlopens the rebound path. Full escape, no caller cooperation.
repro_cases.E_digest_rebound_during_feed: perf_capture.py:38 -> `                digest.update(chunk); digest = hashlib.sha256()` (one-line edit): the gate compares a fresh empty digest, not the fed one

findings.observed: all three cases report status=pass, violations=[]
findings.impact: D fully decouples verified bytes from loaded bytes (the core invariant of the caller_path_sha256 exception). C/E reduce the digest gate to a constant comparison — the loaded file's content provably does not reach the comparison, the exact P1-2 regression class that was supposed to be fixed.
minimal_fix: Count bindings: path_name, digest_name and stream_name must each be bound exactly once in the function (count ast.Assign/AnnAssign/AugAssign targets, ast.NamedExpr targets, for-targets and with optional_vars); any second binding fails closed.

Order: the path_name binding must lexically precede the with-block and all gates; the digest_name binding must lexically precede the with-block; the pinned load must be the last use of path_name (or, equivalently, no statement binding path_name may follow the with-block).
Require the read() call's size argument to be a positive integer constant or a BinOp product of positive integer constants; anything else (0, negative, name, call) fails closed.

findings.title: CDLL(None) handle confinement is a three-pattern blacklist: walrus, container, lambda, return and comprehension escapes all reach arbitrary libc symbols including dlopen
findings.location: tools/audit_core_no_vendor_dll.py: handle scan 529-540 (only Attribute-on-Name, Assign/AnnAssign-from-Name, and getattr(handle) are rejected)
findings.root_cause: The scan blacklists three syntactic shapes instead of whitelisting the handle's allowed contexts. The abstract evaluator returns an untagged _StaticValue for the CDLL result (line 1064-1065), so once the handle leaves its name no downstream rule recognizes it — including the loader-token path, because container/subscript values carry no unknown_owner tag (case H5: dlopen via [libc][0] is also invisible).

repro_cases.H1_handle_escape_walrus: insert at netns_handoff.py:186: `            (h := libc).system(b'id')` — NamedExpr is not Assign; the attribute is on `h`, not `libc`
repro_cases.H2_handle_escape_container: insert: `            [libc][0].system(b'id')` — attribute on a Subscript, not a Name
repro_cases.H3_handle_escape_lambda: insert: `            (lambda: libc)().system(b'id')` — attribute on a Call, not a Name
repro_cases.H4_handle_escape_return: line 194 `return dict(...)` -> `return libc` — Return is not scanned; every caller of enter_namespace receives the whole-process handle
repro_cases.H5_handle_escape_container_dlopen: insert: `            [libc][0].dlopen(b'/tmp/x.so', 2)` — a REAL second native loader, invisible to both the handle scan and rule 6c/load-site tagging
repro_cases.H6_handle_escape_comprehension: insert: `            [x.system(b'id') for x in [libc]]` — comprehension target renames the handle

findings.observed: all six cases report status=pass, violations=[]
findings.impact: The pinned exception 'used only for the Linux setns syscall' is defeated by a one-line insert that borrows the handle to any libc symbol or to dlopen itself — the same severity as the original P1-3, via channels the fix does not model (parameters, containers, closures, return values are all open).
minimal_fix: Replace the blacklist with a parent-aware whitelist: build a parents map once, then for every ast.Name in the module with id == handle require its parent context to be exactly one of (a) the pinned Assign value, (b) the value of an Attribute `.setns` (load) or of `.setns.argtypes`/`.setns.restype` (store), (c) the func of the whitelisted setns call. Any other context — Return, Yield, Call argument, keyword, container element, NamedExpr, Lambda/comprehension body, default value, f-string — fails closed.
Keep the existing three blacklist checks as defense in depth, but the whitelist is the load-bearing rule.
Optional hardening per the original review: tag the pinned handle's abstract value as ctypes_loader so any non-whitelisted use is double-caught by rule 6c/load-site.

findings.title: New regression tests cover token deletion/reorder but not reachability or binding attacks
findings.detail: Covered: `and False` neutralization, raise->pass, load-before-gate reorder, digest.update(b''), decoy-open subscript, direct other-symbol, direct alias. Missing: unreachable-raise (`if False: raise`), outer-condition wrapping, try/except swallow, dead nested def, read(0), path/digest rebinding, walrus/container/lambda/return/comprehension handle escapes.
findings.minimal_fix: Port the 15 bypass mutations from repro_tests.py into PinnedNativeLoadSiteTests as negative cases (each asserting status == 'failed').

findings.title: Claim/docstring overclaim persists
findings.location: tools/audit_core_no_vendor_dll.py: docstring 356-365 ('so every gate dominates the load') and 507-510; claim string
findings.detail: Lexical precedence is not dominance (P1-1 cases B/F/G); 'any alias copy ... fails closed' is true only for direct Assign/AnnAssign aliases. docs/plan/75-core-no-dll-audit.md still states the old single-load-site invariant (already recorded as a known doc gap owned elsewhere; not modified here per scope).
findings.minimal_fix: After tightening the code per P1-1/P1-3, re-verify the wording; otherwise narrow the claim to what the checks prove.

verified_robust: _gate_test_intact bool-only coverage is adequate within the detection shape: `and 0`/`or 1` style non-bool constants either change the top BoolOp type (digest gate requires a bare Compare; path/sha gates require BoolOp-Or -> detection fails -> fail closed) or over-fire an Or-gate (denial direction, not escape). Confirmed by code reading; not counted as a finding.
Both controls behave: unmodified fixture passes; an appended second ctypes.CDLL is rejected twice (unexpected dynamic-load site + forbidden loader reference).
Pinned-line hashes and host-function pinning were held constant in every mutation (asserted in repro_tests.py), so all 15 bypasses are attributable to the new shape logic, not to pin drift.
Real-repo audit and the full pure test suite both pass on the working tree (exit 0 each), so the bypasses are false negatives, not a broken baseline.
